items.title: We have stabilised the present; we must now secure the future’ — Ato Forson
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has called for a decisive break with the economic patterns that have held Ghana back, saying the country must now build on stabilisation to secure lasting prosperity. Speaking during his New Economy engagement with faculty and students at the University of Ghana, Dr Forson said Ghana had reached a moment when public policy must confront the underlying causes of its economic challenges. “We have stabilised the present. Now we must secure the future,” he declared. The Finance Minister framed the next phase of Ghana’s economic journey as a test of the country’s willingness to make decisions that would shape the prospects of future generations. “History does not wait for countries that are afraid to decide,” he said. “There are moments when a nation must make a clear break with old patterns. There are moments when public policy must stop managing symptoms and start changing structures. This is such a moment for Ghana.” His remarks placed structural transformation at the centre of the New Economy agenda, with economic stability serving as the foundation for a more productive economy that creates decent jobs and raises incomes. The challenge, he indicated, is to move beyond addressing immediate pressures and change the conditions that allow those pressures to recur. That ambition, to him, means producing more at home, adding value to what Ghana grows and mines, and expanding opportunities for businesses and workers.

items.title: Tchad : une douzaine de morts lors d’un conflit entre éleveurs et agriculteurs dans le sud-ouest du pays
items.description: Douze personnes sont mortes à la suite d'un conflit entre agriculteurs et éleveurs à la frontière entre les régions de Salamat et de Sila, dans le sud-est du Tchad, ont rapporté ce lundi les médias locaux, citant des sources sécuritaires. La source a indiqué que le bilan provisoire fait état de 12 morts et de trois blessés graves. Selon ces mêmes sources, des représentants des autorités locales, des forces de défense et de sécurité, ainsi que du pouvoir judiciaire, se sont rendus sur place dans la nuit du 18 au 19 octobre afin de gérer la crise. Les sources ont indiqué que le conflit serait probablement dû à un différend concernant la délimitation d'un couloir réservé au déplacement du bétail entre les zones de pâturage.

items.title: CAN FUTSAL 2026 : Hicham Dguig met le cap sur la finale face à l’Angola
items.description: Le sélectionneur national de futsal, Hicham Dguig, a souligné, lundi à Rabat, l’importance de se concentrer pleinement sur la finale de la Coupe d’Afrique des Nations (CAN) Maroc-2026 face à l’Angola, après la large victoire du Maroc contre l’Égypte (6-0) en demi-finale. « La sélection égyptienne n’est pas une équipe facile à battre. C’est une formation pionnière du futsal africain, qui a remporté trois titres continentaux. Nous avons néanmoins démontré que nous étions meilleurs », a déclaré Dguig à l’issue de cette rencontre. Le technicien national a insisté sur la nécessité de tourner rapidement la page de cette demi-finale pour préparer le rendez-vous décisif face à l’Angola, mercredi à Rabat. « Nous devons oublier cette rencontre et nous focaliser sur la finale. L’Angola est une très bonne équipe, dotée de qualités techniques » , a-t-il relevé. Dguig a également réaffirmé l’ambition des Lions de l’Atlas de remporter un quatrième titre continental, avec l’objectif de prendre seuls les commandes du palmarès africain du futsal. Sacré en 2016, 2020 et 2024, le Maroc tentera ainsi de conserver son titre à domicile et de confirmer sa domination sur la scène continentale. The post CAN FUTSAL 2026 : Hicham Dguig met le cap sur la finale face à l’Angola appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Apu returns to The Simpsons with new voice after race row
items.description: The Simpsons character Apu has returned to the show, voiced by a new actor, after almost a decade away amid accusations of racial stereotypes. Apu Nahasapeemapetilon – to give the much-loved shopkeeper his full name – re-appeared in Sunday’s episode on US network Fox, titled The Revengening, but now voiced by India-born, US-raised actor Sunil Malhotra. The character has been seen but not heard around Springfield since the October 2017 episode The Serfsons, and his big return to action had reportedly been a closely guarded secret. Malhotra said in a statement posted on Instagram that it feels like a reclamation. “It truly is his homecoming,” he said. The character, who has been part of the long-running American animated series since 1990, was previously voiced by white actor Hank Azaria, who used a heavy Indian accent. Indian-American comic Hari Kondabolu made a documentary in 2017 titled The Problem With Apu, arguing that the character — a South Asian convenience store clerk — was based on racial stereotypes. The following year, an episode of The Simpsons addressed the controversy surrounding the Indian character for the first time, nodding to the accusations, but some viewers found it insufficient. Others defended the show, saying all its characters were stereotypes. Azaria first announced he was stepping down from the role in 2020, and he later told Dax Shepherd’s Armchair Expert podcast: “Part of me feels like I need to go around to every single Indian person in this country and personally apologise.” ‘Deeply collaborative experience’ Sunil Malhotra has featured in Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi and The Legend of Vox Machina Speaking to Variety ahead of the weekend’s latest episode, Azaria’s replacement Malhotra explained: “When my agent called me about a Simpsons audition, I knew exactly what role it was for, and the idea actually made my stomach sink. “But admittedly, part of me was also curious. It had been eight years since Apu had spoken on the show, and it got me thinking: Did the writers’ room look different now?” The Grey’s Anatomy and The Legend of Korra actor continued: “Could they bring him back in a way that acknowledged and apologised for past mistakes? “Could I make the character my own, and reclaim him in some way? And could they achieve all of that in an unmistakably Simpsons way that didn’t disappoint fans?” After years of Apu having become a mere background character, Malhotra said he spoke with showrunner Matt Selman and co-executive producer Cesar Mazariegos about how they could make the returning fans’ favourite more culturally appropriate for 2026. “It was the beginning of a deeply collaborative experience that I hope is equally satisfying for long-time fans of The Simpsons and for other South Asian kids who, like me, stopped watching at some point along the way.” Apu’s wife, Manjula, will now be voiced Janina Gavankar – who previously appeared in Apple TV’s The Morning Show – taking over from Jan Hooks and Tress MacNeille. In Apu’s haunting comeback episode, a man in a “Daft Monk” Halloween costume — a play on French electro duo Daft Punk — appears to be accidentally killed over and over again by Springfield residents. A year on, he returns to wreak his revenge. Eventually, he summons everyone to the Springfield City Hall, takes off his helmet and reveals himself to be Apu. He then shares his story of having been nearly killed dozens of times, before winding up on The Island of Forgotten Garbage, where he was healed by Dr Nick. “I am the man you left for dead. I am the one you pretended never existed,” he declares. Just as he is about to set the city hall ablaze, Marge Simpson — serving as a thinly veiled mouthpiece for the producers — intervenes, telling him: “Apu, we’re so sorry we left you for dead. Believe me, we wanted to do the right thing.” Her famous bratty son Bart adds: “But we were so scared, and just didn’t know what to do.” Bart’s father Homer then offers to sacrifice himself to save the rest of the town, reminding viewers of how important Apu has been to the town. “You were on our bowling teams, our barbershop quartets, our dad rock cover bands,” said Homer. “We took you for granted. I took you for granted.” The episode will be available to viewers in the UK on Disney+ next week.

items.title: L’ambassadeur de Mauritanie au Tchad a rems ses lettres de créance au président Mohamed Idriss Deby Itno
items.description: L’ambassadeur de Mauritanie au Tchad, Jar O. Inalla a présenté ce lundi, au palais présidentiel de N'Djamena, ses lettres de créance au maréchal Mohamed Idris Déby Itno, président de la République du Tchad, en sa qualité d'ambassadeur extraordinaire et plénipotentiaire de la République islamique de Mauritanie auprès de la République du Tchad avec résidence à Niamey. L’ambassadeur a réaffirmé la volonté de la Mauritanie de renforcer et de développer les relations de coopération existantes entre les deux pays dans divers domaines, afin de répondre aux aspirations des deux nations et de servir leurs intérêts communs. La présidence tchadienne a précisé que « ce diplomate mauritanien, fort d’une expérience diplomatique de plus de 24 ans, a occupé des fonctions au sein de plusieurs missions diplomatiques mauritaniennes, notamment au Japon, en France, en Suisse et en Afrique du Sud. » Il « a également occupé le poste de directeur général des relations internationales et de la coopération au ministère mauritanien des Affaires étrangères à Nouakchott, et a été ambassadeur extraordinaire et plénipotentiaire de son pays en Afrique du Sud, tout en étant accrédité à titre non résident auprès de plusieurs États », selon la même source.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS: NDC says it will remove embattled aspirant if found guilty even after election victory
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) says it will remove its embattled constituency chairmanship aspirant if he is found guilty of sexual abuse, even if he wins the election. Deputy General Secretary Mustapha Gbande said the party had allowed the aspirant to contest while investigations continued. But an election victory would not shield him from sanctions. Speaking on JoyNews’ PM Express on Monday, he said the warning had been made clear to him. “He can now file and proceed,” Mr Gbande said. “The party will remove him and allow him to go and face the law,” he added. The controversy follows Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow . It examines allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School and its headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. The allegations remain under investigation. Mr Gbande confirmed that the aspirant, a long-serving constituency secretary, had appeared before the party’s Functional Executive Committee. The meeting prompted the leadership to reconsider an earlier directive for him to withdraw or face disqualification. “He had already been cleared. He was going to be removed on the basis of the matter,” Mr Gbande said. He explained that the party was taking into account the documentary, a directive by the Education Minister and a Ghana Education Service investigation. The aspirant had also told the leadership that he had filed legal actions against some individuals. Mr Gbande said the party needed to hear his account and avoid undermining those processes. “We have given him an opportunity to state his case, and so I wouldn’t be his PRO.” He said the General Secretary would follow the investigation closely. The party would use the findings to reach an informed decision. Action could also be taken before the investigations end, should substantial findings point to the aspirant’s guilt. “Even if, in the process of the investigation, a substantial determination is made of his guilt, the party will still invite him and take a decision on that matter.” Mr Gbande said any sanctions would reflect the party’s constitution and the public interest. He linked the NDC’s interest in the case to protecting children and restoring confidence in public schools.

items.title: Méouane : Fatma Samoura parraine un projet de complexe sports-études-métiers
items.description: L’ancienne secrétaire générale de la FIFA, Fatma Samoura, a apporté son soutien à un projet de complexe sports-études-métiers à Méouane, dans le département de Tivaouane. Portée par Mamadou Fall, natif de la localité, cette infrastructure sera construite sur un site de 8 à 15 hectares, à proximité du tracé de la future autoroute à péage, dont la livraison est prévue en juillet 2027. Le complexe comprendra deux terrains de football, deux terrains de football à sept, une piste d’athlétisme, une piscine, des terrains de basketball, de handball et de tennis, ainsi qu’une salle de gymnastique. Il abritera également des salles d’études, des ateliers de formation aux métiers de la couture, de la menuiserie et de la mécanique, un daara, une mosquée et des dortoirs. Accompagnée d’une délégation comprenant d’anciens internationaux sénégalais, Fatma Samoura a remis une contribution de 5 millions de FCFA pour le démarrage du projet, dont le coût global est estimé à plusieurs milliards de FCFA. Le maire de Méouane, Cheikh Sall, et le sous-préfet ont, pour leur part, assuré le promoteur de leur accompagnement. Mamadou Fall a expliqué que le projet vise à prendre en charge des jeunes âgés de 11 à 13 ans, notamment ceux sortis des daaras ou déscolarisés, afin de leur offrir un encadrement scolaire et sportif, tout en leur permettant d’apprendre un métier. « C’est un centre comme Génération Foot ou Diambars, mais avec une particularité : le sport et les métiers. Il y aura des études et l’apprentissage d’un métier », a expliqué le promoteur, originaire de Touba Fall, dans la commune de Méouane. Selon lui, le projet sera réalisé en partenariat avec Génération Foot et d’autres partenaires nationaux et internationaux, dont les noms seront dévoilés lors de la cérémonie de pose de la première pierre. La capacité d’accueil initiale du complexe est estimée entre 50 et 100 pensionnaires, avec une montée en puissance progressive pour atteindre 200 à 300 jeunes. Mamadou Fall a salué l’accompagnement du maire de Méouane et de l’ancienne secrétaire générale de la FIFA, Fatma Samoura, dont le soutien constitue une étape importante dans la concrétisation de cette initiative. Ibrahima NDIAYE Correspondant

items.title: N4,000/$ Exchange Rate: NDC asks why refineries are not working
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has faulted the Federal Government’s warning that a return to petrol subsidy could push the naira to between N3,000 and N4,000 per dollar, demanding explanations for the failure of the country’s refineries to operate effectively. The party also questioned why Nigeria had mortgaged a sizeable portion of its crude oil to secure foreign loans, alleging that the arrangement had affected the country’s ability to supply the Dangote Refinery with sufficient crude oil to meet domestic demand. The NDC’s National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, made the remarks while reacting to comments by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, who warned against a return to petrol subsidy. Oyedele had said reinstating the subsidy could trigger capital flight, undermine investor confidence and weaken the naira to N3,000, N3,500 or even N4,000 to the dollar. In response, Director said the government should address the underlying problems in the petroleum sector rather than focus solely on the potential consequences of restoring the subsidy. “The most important aspect of the subsidy conversation is not yet addressed. Why are our refineries not working? Why did the APC government mortgage a sizeable portion of our crude oil to take foreign loans to the extent that we are unable to supply Dangote Refinery the needed crude oil to satisfy domestic consumption and demand?” he asked. He argued that addressing the challenges affecting domestic refining and what he described as criminality in the subsidy regime would make the minister’s warning unnecessary. “If all these and the criminality in the subsidy regime are addressed, the doomsday prediction of the Minister of Finance would not be necessary,” Director said. Oyedele had issued the warning during a press briefing at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, on Monday. The minister said investors had repeatedly questioned whether the Federal Government would abandon its economic reforms ahead of the next election cycle. He added that President Bola Tinubu had maintained that the national budget had made no provision for petrol subsidy since June 2023, insisting that the subsidy had therefore been removed. items.title: Mahama visits Kufuor to discuss national, global affairs
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has visited former President John Agyekum Kufuor at his residence to enquire about his well-being and exchange views on issues affecting Ghana and the international community. The meeting took place on Monday, October 19, with President Mahama later sharing details of the engagement on his Facebook page. “I passed by the residence of President J.A Kufuor this afternoon to check on him and find out how he’s doing and also discuss some national and international issues,” he wrote. Photographs accompanying the post showed the two former political rivals smiling and engaging during the visit. The meeting brought together the sitting President and his predecessor from the New Patriotic Party (NPP), who governed Ghana from 2001 to 2009. The engagement also offered an opportunity for the two leaders to interact outside the formal setting of official state functions. Mr Kufuor, who served as Ghana’s President for two terms, handed over power to the late President John Evans Atta Mills in January 2009, following the NDC’s victory in the 2008 general election. President Mahama, who first became President in 2012, returned to office after winning the 2024 general election.

items.title: At 50: Brand refresh raises questions about heritage, consumer loyalty
items.description: By Chioma Obinna As competition in Nigeria’s non-alcoholic beverage market continues to evolve, Maltina, one of the country’s longstanding malt drink brands, has unveiled a refreshed visual identity to mark its 50th anniversary, retaining its familiar taste while introducing redesigned packaging across its product range. The new identity, unveiled by Nigerian Breweries Plc last week, features updated designs across glass bottles, cans and PET bottles, with enhanced gold elements and a stronger orange colour scheme aimed at giving the brand a more contemporary appearance. The redesign highlights a broader challenge facing established consumer brands: how to modernise their appearance to appeal to changing consumer preferences without losing the familiarity and trust built over decades. For Maltina, which has been part of Nigeria’s beverage market since 1976, the anniversary presents an opportunity to reinforce its heritage while repositioning the brand for a new generation of consumers. However, beyond the visual changes, the success of the refresh will depend on how consumers respond to the new packaging and whether the brand can sustain its relevance in an increasingly competitive market. Other features of the refreshed identity include a gold crown cork, brighter sunrays, a more prominent golden barley icon, a bolder calcium coin and a “Since 1976” heritage mark, underscoring the brand’s five-decade history in Nigeria. Despite the packaging changes, Nigerian Breweries said Maltina’s familiar taste and nutritional composition remain unchanged. The company said the drink is fortified with calcium, with one 33cl bottle providing the equivalent of half a glass of milk. The brand is also endorsed by the Nutrition Society of Nigeria as a non-alcoholic drink rich in Vitamin A. Speaking on the refreshed identity, the Marketing Director of Nigerian Breweries Plc, Sarah Agha, said the redesign was intended to keep the brand relevant to contemporary consumers while preserving its heritage. “For 50 years, Maltina has grown alongside generations of Nigerians. This refreshed identity is an evolution of a much-loved brand, designed to keep Maltina fresh, relevant and connected to today’s consumers while preserving the nourishing taste they know and trust,” Agha said. Her remarks reflect the company’s effort to balance continuity with change, maintaining the product attributes familiar to existing consumers while introducing a new visual experience that could attract younger buyers. For established brands, packaging plays an important role in consumer recognition, influencing how products stand out on retail shelves and how customers relate to them. A redesign, therefore, must do more than create a different appearance; it must preserve the identity that consumers associate with the product. Maltina’s decision to retain its taste and nutritional composition while updating its packaging suggests that the company is seeking to refresh its market appeal without altering the product experience on which its reputation has been built. As part of the relaunch, Nigerian Breweries is introducing a consumer engagement campaign tagged “What’s Your Word?”, inviting Nigerians to describe their first impressions of the new packaging in one word. According to Agha, the campaign is intended to involve consumers in shaping the brand’s next chapter by encouraging them to share their reactions to the refreshed identity. “This relaunch is about more than a new pack. It is an invitation for Nigerians to help shape the next chapter of a brand that has been part of their lives for five decades. We look forward to hearing the words the new Maltina inspires,” she added. The post At 50: Brand refresh raises questions about heritage, consumer loyalty appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Catholic bishops declare nationwide fasting, prayer
items.description: The Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria, CBCN, has declared a nationwide prayer and fasting programme to promote free, fair, credible and peaceful elections in 2027. The programme, themed ‘Let Justice and Peace Flow’, is drawn from Amos 5:24. The bishops announced the initiative in a statement signed by their President, Archbishop Matthew Ndagoso, and Secretary, Bishop Peter Odetoyinbo, yesterday in Abuja. They said the programme was necessary as Nigeria approached the 2027 general elections amid recurring challenges of electoral violence, rigging, vote-buying and ethno-religious divisions. The bishops urged dioceses, parishes, church societies, prayer groups, families and individuals to participate actively in the spiritual exercise. They said the initiative was aimed at seeking God’s guidance for electoral officials and security personnel to discharge their responsibilities faithfully, while inspiring citizens to vote conscientiously and discouraging electoral malpractice and violence. According to the statement, all parishes would observe October 31 and November 28 as days of prayer and fasting for Nigeria. Activities would include fasting, the Rosary procession, Holy Mass and the recitation of the CBCN prayer for the 2027 elections. The bishops also designated December 8, the Solemnity of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary, as a nationwide diocesan day of prayer. The programme would begin with Holy Mass at 3 p.m., presided over by the diocesan bishop, during which a pastoral letter titled “2027 Elections: Call to Responsible Choice and Action” would be read. The Mass would be followed by a Rosary procession to the cathedral at 4:30 p.m. and conclude with Eucharistic Benediction. The statement further declared January 15, 2027, the eve of the general elections, a nationwide parish day of prayer and fasting. The bishops urged Nigerians to reject tribalism, corruption, bribery and voter apathy, while encouraging citizens to vote and protect their votes peacefully. They called for a credible electoral process free from rancour and bloodshed. The post Catholic bishops declare nationwide fasting, prayer appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Jigawa NUJ secures release of six inmates
items.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Jigawa State Council, has secured the release of six inmates from the Gumel Correctional Centre by paying fines imposed on them by the courts. The intervention was part of activities marking the council’s maiden Press Week, aimed at promoting humanitarian services and supporting vulnerable members of society. This was disclosed in a statement jointly signed by the NUJ State Chairman, Comrade Isma’il Ibrahim Dutse, and the Council Secretary, Comrade Aminu Umar Shuwajo. According to the statement, the six beneficiaries had remained in custody because they could not afford to pay the fines imposed on them as alternatives to imprisonment. They were identified as Musa Ilu, popularly known as Gwaska; Umar Sani; Inusa Lawan; Hassan Shu’aibu; Nuhu Hassan; and Suraja Tahir, also known as Chanko. The union said the intervention reflected its commitment to giving back to society and supporting people facing difficult circumstances. In a related development, the NUJ delegation visited the Dutse Correctional Centre, where it donated essential items to improve the welfare of inmates. The items included cartons of Maggi Star seasoning, May soap, Klin detergent and sanitary pads. Presenting the items, Dutse said the visit was part of activities lined up to mark the council’s maiden Press Week. Receiving the donations, the Officer-in-Charge of the centre, CSC Muhammad Nazir, commended the union for the humanitarian gesture. Nazir described the intervention as the first of its kind by journalists in the state and acknowledged the media’s role as a partner in societal development. He assured the union of continued cordial relations with the correctional service and urged other unions and organisations in the state to emulate the gesture. items.title: Bruxelles : six arrestations après le meurtre d'un policier d'origine marocaine
items.description: L'émotion est vive en Belgique après l'assassinat d'un officier de police d'origine marocaine, Nordine El Talbi – 41 ans, tué par balle lors d'une intervention la semaine dernière dans la commune de Jette, à Bruxelles. Lors d'une conférence de presse tenue dimanche, le procureur du Roi à Bruxelles, Julien Moinil, a annoncé l'arrestation de six suspects impliqués dans cette affaire qui secoue l'opinion publique et le corps sécuritaire belge. La traque internationale orchestrée par les services de police a permis d'interpeller trois des suspects à Almería, en Espagne, alors qu'ils tentaient vraisemblablement de s'enfuir vers le Maroc. Un quatrième individu a été intercepté dans une gare parisienne, tandis que les deux derniers membres du groupe avaient été arrêtés à Bruxelles peu après les faits. Tous originaires de la capitale belge et connus des services de justice pour des affaires de stupéfaction et de grand banditisme, ils font désormais l'objet de procédures d'extradition de la part des autorités belges vers la France et l'Espagne. Le drame s'est déroulé dans la nuit de lundi à mardi derniers, alors que la victime et ses coéquipiers traquaient un véhicule volé à Tubize. Repérant la voiture vers minuit sur l'avenue Carton de Wiart à Jette, l'officier s'est approché pour inspecter le véhicule avant d'être mortellement touché à la tête par un coup de feu tiré depuis l'intérieur de l'habitacle. Le procureur a précisé que cinq personnes se trouvaient à bord du véhicule volé, où de la drogue a également été retrouvée, et que les analyses balistiques ainsi que les prélèvements d'ADN détermineront avec précision l'auteur du tir mortel, tout en soulignant la responsabilité collective de l'ensemble du groupe. Cette tragédie ravive l'inquiétude grandissante au sein des forces de l'ordre belges face à la prolifération des armes à feu et à la violence accrue des réseaux criminels envers les policiers dans l'exercice de leurs fonctions. Hommage appuyé « Courageux, intègre, professionnel, investi, jovial, collégial, souriant, respectueux et extraordinairement apprécié ». C'est par cette série de qualités que Michel Goovaerts, chef de corps de la zone de police Bruxelles-Capitale/Ixelles (PolBru), a rendu hommage vendredi à Nordine El Talbi, inspecteur principal de police et membre de la Brigade anti-agression (BAA). Plus 1.000 policiers sont venus de toute la Belgique se sont rassemblés au Cinquantenaire. L'émotion se lisait sur les visages. Parmi eux, des membres des unités spéciales, des policiers en tenue, d'autres en civil, des jeunes en formation et des cadets. La Musique royale des Guides a accompagné la cérémonie, en présence de nombreuses autorités politiques et judiciaires. « Cette cérémonie n'aurait jamais dû avoir lieu », a déclaré le bourgmestre de Bruxelles, Philippe Close (PS). « Il aurait dû rentrer chez lui, retrouver les siens », a-t-il déploré. items.title: Isaac Opoku raises Ghana’s flag high in London with Commonwealth honour
items.description: Ghanaian youth leader Isaac Opoku has been received by the Ghana High Commissioner to the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth Secretary General in London, as he celebrates being named one of the QECT 100 Young Leaders 2026. Isaac, founder of the Starlight Foundation, visited Her Excellency Mrs Sabah Zita Benson, Ghana’s High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, and Her Excellency Shirley Ayorkor Botchwey, Secretary-General of the Commonwealth, alongside two fellow Ghanaian awardees. During the visit, he shared his personal story, explained why he started the Foundation, and spoke about its work with children and families across Ghana. The three young leaders also presented the award plaques they had received. The High Commissioner said she was impressed by their work and proud that they had raised the flag of Ghana high within the Commonwealth. Madam Botchwey, the first Ghanaian and the first African woman to serve as Commonwealth Secretary-General, spoke of her pride in seeing young Ghanaians recognised at this level and of her belief in the work they are doing. “To sit before two Ghanaian women leading at the very top and hear them say they are proud of us was something I will carry for a long time,” Isaac said. “This award is for every child in Ghana who has been told their dreams are too big.” The QECT 100 Young Leaders Award, given by the Queen Elizabeth II Commonwealth Trust, marks what would have been the 100th birthday of the late Queen Elizabeth II. Isaac was first named an awardee on 21 April 2026 and received the award in person this October at a ceremony at Asprey in Mayfair, London. As an awardee, he was also invited to a reception at St James’s Palace, where he spoke with His Majesty King Charles III and Her Majesty Queen Camilla, and met Her Royal Highness The Duchess of Gloucester. For Isaac, the recognition goes back to where it all began. Born and raised in Accra by a single mother, he founded the Starlight Foundation in 2018 to support children living and working on the streets and their families. Through more than 50 initiatives, the Foundation has since reached over 40,000 people. Its Centre for Design and Innovation in Accra offers a STEAM model built for vulnerable communities, and its learning resources on menstrual hygiene, personal safety, digital literacy and children’s rights are now used in schools across Ghana. Its flagship programme, Menso Meka Ho Bi, meaning “I’m also privileged”, works with whole families so that children are not supported in isolation but within homes that can sustain their progress. The Foundation also contributed to the United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child’s General Comment 27, giving Ghanaian voices a part in shaping global children’s rights policy. This year, at the invitation of the National Youth Authority, it submitted written input to Ghana’s first National Action Plan on Youth, Peace and Security. The QECT honour adds to a growing list of recognition for Isaac and the Starlight Foundation. In 2023, Isaac was named Man of Excellence in Philanthropy at the Ghana Business and Entrepreneurs Awards. In 2024, he received the Bright Futures Award for Community Impact and was named Young Philanthropist of the Year by Humanitarian Awards Global. The Starlight Foundation was named Leading Youth-Led Education NGO 2025 by Acquisition International in the UK, and this year it was named Best Child Welfare & Empowerment NPO 2026 – Ghana at the 9th annual African Excellence Awards by AI Global Media, also in the UK. The Foundation’s Let Her Know initiative has been nominated by the Ghana National Commission for UNESCO for the 2026 UNESCO Prize for Girls’ and Women’s Education. In addition, Starlight has received approval from the YOUNGO LCOY Working Group to host a Local Conference of Youth (LCOY) in Ghana in 2026, joining a global network of youth-led climate conferences recognised under the YOUNGO framework under the United Nations. The Foundation has also submitted inputs to the United Nations on Gen-Z Activism and Civic Space and on the Post-2030 Youth Education and Learning Agenda, contributing young Ghanaian voices to global policy discussions. As a graduate of Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Isaac began his career at the Ghana Audit Service, where he developed the original concept for the Citizen Eye mobile application. His communications work with Parliamentary Network Africa later helped build the public pressure that contributed to Parliament passing the Right to Information Bill in 2019. Now based in the UK, he was elected this year as a councillor on Campbell Park Community Council in Milton Keynes and volunteers as a Peer Mentor with Connection Support. He also holds a master’s degree from Cranfield University among other qualifications. His message to young Ghanaians at home and abroad is simple. “Do not wait to be chosen,” he said. “Start with what you have, serve the people around you and stay consistent. Ghana has so much talent. We just need to believe it is enough.” With the Starlight Foundation now planning to expand across West Africa, Isaac says the work at home will remain at the heart of everything he does.

items.title: ‘An unacceptable breach’ – Hawa Koomson warns over alleged failure to act on Obuasi SHTS abuse complaints
items.description: NPP National Women’s Organiser has warned that school authorities’ alleged failure to act on sexual abuse complaints at Obuasi Senior High Technical School would amount to “an unacceptable breach” of their responsibility to protect students, if established. In a statement issued on Monday, Mavis Hawa Koomson demanded an independent criminal investigation into allegations involving the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. Her intervention follows media reports, including an investigation by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni, concerning approximately 19 female students. According to her statement, the students have recounted alleged rape, sexual harassment, sexual assault and other forms of abuse. Ms Koomson expressed particular concern over reports that some complaints reached school authorities as far back as March 2026. She said the alleged absence of meaningful action had left serious questions about the protection of affected students. If established, she said, such inaction would constitute grave negligence of the school authorities’ duty of care. “No institution entrusted with educating and developing young people should compromise their safety, dignity, and psychological well-being.” She called on the Criminal Investigations Department of the Ghana Police Service to conduct a swift, thorough, independent and transparent investigation. Where sufficient evidence is established, she urged prosecutorial authorities to pursue legal processes regardless of the political affiliation, social standing or institutional position of anyone implicated. “A child knows no political party colours. We must never subordinate the dignity, safety, and protection of our children to partisan considerations.” Ms Koomson also raised concerns about reports of possible intimidation, victimisation and reprisals against affected students and their families. She demanded measures to protect their identities, guarantee their safety and shield those reporting alleged abuse from retaliation. She asked the Ministry of Gender, Children, and Social Protection and the Ghana Education Service to coordinate counselling, psychological support, medical care and other protective assistance. Beyond the investigation, she called for a comprehensive GES review of child protection policies and rules governing the conduct of teachers, headmasters and school administrators. She also appealed to women across the country, particularly the Vice President, to support efforts to secure justice and strengthen safeguards for girls. “Justice must be pursued without fear or favour. Accountability must know no political boundaries, and the protection of our children must remain a shared national responsibility.”

items.title: Tinubu extends tenures of Immigration, Correctional Service Chiefs
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has approved 18-month tenure extensions for Sylvester Ndidi Nwakuche, Controller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service, and Kemi Nanna Nandap, Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service. Following the approval, Nwakuche’s tenure will now end on May 26, 2028, while Nandap’s will end on June 30, 2028. The approval, which followed a recommendation by the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, is aimed at addressing succession gaps in both services and giving their respective boards sufficient time to appoint successors. President Tinubu commended Nwakuche and Nandap for the reforms achieved under their leadership and charged them to consolidate the gains. Tinubu nominated Nwakuche as Controller-General of the Nigerian Correctional Service in December 2024. The Senate confirmed his appointment in March 2025. The President nominated Kemi Nanna Nandap as Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service on February 21, 2024. The Senate confirmed her appointment on March 1, 2024. items.title: Buhari: If a general couldn’t wipe out insecurity, spare Tinubu —Yari
items.description: The Director-General of All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has said President Bola Tinubu should not be blamed solely for the widespread insecurity in the country. Yari, who stated this during a visit to Kebbi, where he met with Governor Nasir Idris, traditional rulers and other party leaders in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State, yesterday, said ex-President Muhammadu Buhari, a retired general, did his best but could not tackle insecurity completely. He acknowledged the security challenges facing the country but maintained that the Tinubu administration was making efforts to address them. He recalled that former President Muhammadu Buhari, a retired Army general, had also made efforts to tackle insecurity during his administration, although the challenge was not completely eliminated. “If a retired general did his best but could not completely tackle insecurity, what do you expect of President Tinubu, who is not a general? Nevertheless, the President has done his utmost best to address the security challenges confronting the country,” he said. Yari also urged Nigerians to reflect on their relationship with God, noting that addressing insecurity required collective responsibility alongside government efforts. He commended the governor and other APC leaders for their efforts in mobilising support for the party, expressing confidence that their collective commitment would ensure victory for Tinubu and other APC candidates in 2027. “We are leading the campaign for the President’s re-election and other candidates of our party. We appreciate you for bringing the emirs together under one umbrella at the Emir of Gwandu’s palace. “We recognise what you are doing as governors and your contributions towards ensuring victory for our party in 2027,” he said. Yari said the campaign council would work with all individuals and groups committed to Tinubu’s re-election, regardless of their positions, to achieve the party’s objectives. He expressed confidence in the APC’s chances in Kebbi, citing the support observed during his visit to the state. On the economy, he said the hardship being experienced by Nigerians was not peculiar to the country, adding that inflation had declined and fertiliser prices reduced. He said the federal government was implementing measures to ease the burden on citizens, including cash transfers to vulnerable households. According to him, the measures are intended to strengthen the economy and improve living conditions for Nigerians. Yari acknowledged that governments worldwide faced challenges, citing the United States and Saudi Arabia as examples of countries still working to address various national concerns. He urged Nigerians to appreciate the efforts of the Tinubu administration and support its development agenda. In his response, Governor Idris described the visit by the PCC delegation as a welcome development, expressing happiness over the gathering of APC leaders and traditional rulers to receive the team. He said the emirs decided to come together at the palace to demonstrate solidarity and welcome the delegation. Idris said Kebbi had benefited from federal government projects under Tinubu’s administration, adding that the development initiatives had strengthened the state’s support for the President. “We have no reason not to support the President. We have prominent leaders such as Sen. Atiku Bagudu, Sen. Adamu Aliero and Amb. Saidu Dakingari. “You have seen the people of Kebbi and their overwhelming support. We are for the APC and we are for President Tinubu,” Idris said. The governor expressed confidence that the state would continue to support the APC ahead of the 2027 general elections. items.title: Hawa Koomson demands independent probe into alleged abuse of 19 Obuasi SHS girls
items.description: The National Women’s Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Mavis Hawa Koomson, has called for a swift, independent and transparent investigation into allegations of sexual abuse involving 19 female students of Obuasi Senior High School (SHS). She has urged the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service to investigate the allegations and ensure that anyone found culpable faces the appropriate legal processes. The call follows an investigative report by Joy FM’s Manasseh Azure Awuni, concerning allegations of rape, sexual harassment, sexual assault and other forms of abuse involving the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai. In a statement issued on October 19, 2026, Hawa Koomson said the reports were particularly disturbing because some of the alleged incidents had reportedly been brought to the attention of school authorities as far back as March 2026, without meaningful action to protect the students. She stressed that the allegations must be investigated thoroughly and that accountability should not be influenced by political affiliation, social standing or the position of anyone implicated. “A child knows no political party colours. We must never subordinate the dignity, safety, and protection of our children to partisan considerations,” she said. The allegations have not been established, and the call for an investigation is intended to ensure that the facts are determined through due process. Protect students from reprisals Hawa Koomson expressed concern over reports of possible intimidation, victimisation and reprisals against the students and their families. She called for measures to protect the identities of the affected students, guarantee their safety and preserve their dignity throughout any investigative and judicial proceedings. She also urged authorities to provide a safe and confidential environment for other potential victims to report similar experiences without fear of retaliation. The National Women’s Organiser called on the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection and the Ghana Education Service (GES) to work with child protection organisations and other relevant support groups to provide assistance to the students and their families. The support, she said, should include professional counselling, trauma-informed psychological care, medical attention and other protective measures. She further urged state institutions and civil society organisations to ensure that the welfare of the students remained central to every intervention. GES urged to review safeguards Beyond the immediate allegations, Hawa Koomson called on the GES to undertake a comprehensive review of child protection and safeguarding policies in schools. She said the situation raised questions about reporting procedures, supervision, professional conduct and accountability within educational institutions. She called for effective and enforceable systems to prevent sexual abuse and exploitation, respond promptly to complaints and protect students’ physical and psychological well-being. Hawa Koomson said the best interests of the child must remain paramount, in line with the Children’s Act, 1998 (Act 560). “Our girls must feel safe, protected, respected and empowered within the very institutions established to nurture their potential and secure their future. No girl should ever be compelled to sacrifice her dignity, safety or fundamental rights in pursuit of education,” she said. She also appealed to women across the country, particularly the Vice-President, to take a keen and sustained interest in the matter and use their influence to support efforts to secure justice for the affected students. Call for national action Hawa Koomson urged state institutions, traditional and religious leaders, child protection advocates and the general public to support a credible investigative process. She said the matter went beyond political affiliations and institutional loyalties, describing the protection of children as a shared national responsibility. “Justice must be pursued without fear or favour. Accountability must know no political boundaries, and the protection of our children must remain a shared national responsibility,” she said.

items.title: Obuasi SHTS: NDC reverses withdrawal directive, allows embattled chairman aspirant to contest
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has reversed its directive, asking embattled Obuasi Senior High Technical School headmaster Zakaria Abdulai to withdraw from the constituency chairmanship race. Deputy General Secretary Mustapha Gbande says he can now file and contest while investigations into sexual abuse allegations against him continue. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, he confirmed the reversal. But he warned that winning the election would not shield the aspirant from removal. “He can now file and proceed,” Mr Gbande said. The decision follows Abdulai’s appearance before the party’s Functional Executive Committee. Gbande said the party needed to hear his response before deciding its next move. “Indeed, it is true. Those were preliminary directives that were taken.” The host had asked whether an earlier withdrawal directive still stood. The party’s deputy communications director announced on The Probe that Abdulai would be disqualified if he contested. Mr Gbande said the committee reconsidered that position after reviewing the processes already underway. These include a ministerial directive and an investigation by the Ghana Education Service. Abdulai also told the committee he had issued writs against some individuals connected to the matter. Mr Gbande said he was unsure whether the suits concerned defamation. The allegations are the subject of Manasseh Azure Awuni’s documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow . It examines alleged sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School. Click here to Watch the documentary . Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu directed the GES on October 13 to suspend Abdulai pending investigations. He also requested an inquiry from the police Criminal Investigation Department. Mr Gbande said the party wanted to protect the aspirant’s rights while allowing those processes to run. “We have given him an opportunity to state his case, and so I wouldn’t be his PRO.” He said the General Secretary would follow the investigation closely. The findings would guide the party’s next decision. Mr Gbande also made clear that permission to contest did not settle the allegations. “He would have to go and make his own case,” he said. According to Gbande, the leadership warned Abdulai that he could be removed even after winning the election if found guilty. Substantial findings during the investigation could also prompt further action. The long-serving constituency secretary is seeking to become constituency chairman. “But in the meantime, we think that, given the nature of the processes that have been triggered, it is only prudent and right that the party proceed with caution and follow the story keenly as it unravels.”

items.title: Doctors top global trust rankings as politicians, influencers come last
items.description: By Sola Ogundipe Medical doctors, scientists and teachers are the most trusted professions globally, while politicians and social media influencers rank among the least trusted, according to a survey of 23,530 online adults under 75 across 32 countries. The survey, known as the Ipsos Global Trustworthiness Index 2026, conducted by Ipsos, an international market research and public opinion polling company, showed that doctors lead the rankings, with 58 percent of respondents expressing trust in them, followed by scientists at 56 percent and teachers at 54 percent. Restaurant serving staff ranked fourth at 44 percent, followed by the armed forces at 43 percent. Police officers, judges and ordinary men and women each recorded 38 percent, while lawyers received 31 percent. Television news anchors recorded 30 percent, while pollsters and clergy or priests each scored 29 percent. Taxi drivers and civil servants followed at 28 percent. Journalists and bankers each recorded 27 percent, while business leaders scored 26 percent. At the lower end, government ministers recorded 20 per cent, followed by advertising executives at 19 per cent. Social media influencers and politicians generally ranked last, with 15 per cent each. The percentages represent the share of respondents expressing trust in each profession or group, not those selecting it as their single most trusted occupation. The precise survey question and response options should be verified against the original Ipsos report. The findings highlight a marked contrast between trust in health and scientific professionals and confidence in political figures and social surveys. items.title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support, says court filing
items.description: A Saudi national charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI’s meeting rooms has been accused of having “considerable support” from the Saudi government, according to a court filing in California. US prosecutors claimed Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked for the AI firm, was in “frequent communication… with a member of the Saudi royal family”, and said a member of the country’s military paid for a one-way flight to Saudi Arabia for his wife and son after his arrest. The 35-year-old engineer was deemed a flight risk on Monday and denied bail pending trial. The Saudi government did not immediately respond to BBC requests for comment. Alfozan had worked at OpenAI for about a year before he allegedly attempted to plant an audio recorder. The AI company discovered the device, which was plugged into the back of a TV in a conference meeting room and covered up with toilet paper, on 30 September. A camera was placed in the room and on 5 October, Alfozan was filmed entering and appearing to look behind the television where the audio recorder had been inserted. He was arrested by the FBI on 9 October and his contract with OpenAI was terminated. The court filing claimed the suspect’s alleged conduct could pose “a danger to the national security of the United States”, because executives from the tech firm met with government officials in the room during the days the device was believed to have been installed. It said Alfozan’s arrest came three days before he was scheduled to fly from San Francisco to Riyadh on a one-way itinerary with his wife and son. Following the arrest, the document claims the defendant’s wife told FBI agents who interviewed her that “her US visa was expiring” and so she and her son were “permanently moving back to Saudi Arabia”, and her husband intended to do the same. On 10 October, the day after Alfozan was arrested, his wife and son flew from San Francisco to Doha, Qatar. They travelled on a one-way business class ticket booked and paid for by a Saudi military official. “Ultimately, the defendant has little incentive to remain in the United States to see this case through,” the prosecutors argued. US district judge Alex Tse on Monday denied Alfozan’s attorneys request for his release on bail, saying “there is a risk of non-appearance that is significant”. The FBI investigation is ongoing. Alfozan was scheduled to ‌appear ⁠in federal court in San Francisco later on Monday. If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 (£188,000) fine.

items.title: CRIEF : 7 ans de prison requis contre deux huissiers, Ecobank réclame 5 millions de dollars
items.description: Le parquet spécial près la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF) a requis, ce lundi 19 octobre 2026, sept ans d’emprisonnement ferme contre Mes Sory Daouda Camara et Mandiou Sangaré, poursuivis dans une affaire opposant Ecobank Guinée à plusieurs professionnels du droit. De son côté, la banque réclame 5 millions de dollars et 20 milliards de francs guinéens à titre de dommages et intérêts. À l’audience consacrée aux réquisitions et plaidoiries, le conseil d’Ecobank Guinée, Me Antoine Pépé Lama, a accusé les deux huissiers d’avoir contribué à la production d’un document qu’il estime faux et qui aurait conduit à la condamnation de la banque par la Cour commune de justice et d’arbitrage (CCJA). « Aujourd’hui, il ne reste plus qu’à rétablir Ecobank Guinée dans ses droits », a plaidé l’avocat, sollicitant la condamnation solidaire des deux prévenus au paiement des dommages et intérêts réclamés par la banque. Représentant le parquet spécial, Pierre Segbe Kamano a requis sept ans d’emprisonnement ferme et une amende de 50 millions de francs guinéens contre chacun des deux huissiers. Il a également demandé que Mes Sory Daouda Camara et Mandiou Sangaré, ainsi que Me Halimé Saad Chaloub, avocate également mise en cause dans le dossier, soient interdits d’exercer leur profession pendant trois ans. De leur côté, les avocats de la défense ont contesté les accusations portées contre leurs clients, dénonçant une procédure qu’ils jugent orientée et déséquilibrée. « C’est une procédure téléguidée. C’est une procédure orientée. L’équilibre entre les parties est largement rompu dans cette procédure », a plaidé la défense, estimant que cette affaire, qui remonte à 2018, aurait dû faire l’objet d’une information judiciaire plutôt que d’être traitée selon la procédure de flagrant délit. Pour Me Mory Doumbouya, les infractions reprochées à ses clients ne sont pas constituées. « Il n’y a pas de faux, ni escroquerie, ni complicité dans cette procédure », a-t-il soutenu, invitant la cour à ne pas suivre les réquisitions du parquet. Poursuivis notamment pour des faits présumés de faux et usage de faux, d’escroquerie au jugement et de complicité, Mes Sory Daouda Camara et Mandiou Sangaré sont en détention préventive depuis le 29 septembre 2026. À l’issue des réquisitions et des plaidoiries, la décision de la CRIEF est désormais attendue.

items.title: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
items.description: Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage with French former tennis player Gaël Monfils, citing the emotional impact of the war in her country. The 32-year-old, who is ranked number six in the world, wrote in a heartfelt Instagram post about the effect of the conflict and “what the war has done to me inside”. “This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share,” she wrote, saying “I need to find my way back to myself”. Svitolina said she felt she could not do that within her marriage. She said her husband Monfils, 40, “listened” and “respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget”. “Some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you,” the four-time Grand Slam semi-finalist wrote. It was “the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love”, Svitolina said. “Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me,” Svitolina, who grew up in Odesa, said. Ukraine’s Black Sea port city has been heavily bombed by Russia throughout the war. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. “What you didn’t see were the sleepless nights, the doubts, and the feeling of slowly losing myself.” The tennis power couple married in 2021 and have one child together, a four-year-old daughter named Skai. Svitolina said her daughter “will always come first”, adding “our marriage is ending, but our family is not”. Monfils, a former world number six, was expected to play the final tournament of his career at next month’s Paris Masters in an emotional farewell. However, the two-time Grand Slam semi-finalist’s retirement was effectively confirmed last week when he was added to the International Tennis Integrity Authority’s list of retired players. Once a player withdraws from anti-doping protocols, they are ineligible to compete in professional tournaments. Monfils, who won 13 titles on the ATP Tour, is preparing to start a new career in finance after joining a Swiss wealth management firm.

items.title: Agriculture en Guinée : à Tindo, cinq jours de formation pour renforcer les capacités des responsables agricoles (du 12 au 16 octobre 2026)
items.description: Faranah, le 19 octobre 2026 – Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de la Campagne agricole 2026-2027, le ministère de l’Agriculture, à travers la Direction nationale de l’Agriculture, a organisé une session de formation destinée au renforcement des capacités des responsables régionaux, préfectoraux et communaux de l’Agriculture et de l’Élevage. Cette rencontre s’est tenue du 12 au 16 octobre 2026 au Centre de vulgarisation agricole de Tindo, dans la préfecture de Faranah, autour des enjeux de la planification, du suivi et de l’évaluation des activités agricoles. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans la dynamique de modernisation du secteur agricole guinéen et de renforcement des mécanismes de gouvernance, afin d’améliorer la coordination des interventions sur le terrain et de favoriser une gestion plus efficace des programmes et projets agricoles. Renforcer les compétences pour une agriculture plus performante La formation a réuni huit directeurs régionaux, trente-trois directeurs préfectoraux et treize directeurs communaux de l’Agriculture et de l’Élevage. L’objectif principal était de doter ces responsables des compétences nécessaires pour mieux planifier les activités, coordonner les interventions, maîtriser les moyens disponibles et assurer un suivi rigoureux des résultats obtenus. Dans un contexte marqué par le lancement officiel de la Campagne agricole 2026-2027, le 8 avril dernier, sous le slogan « Nourrir la Guinée avec nos propres ressources », le renforcement des capacités des acteurs institutionnels apparaît comme un levier essentiel pour accroître la production et la productivité agricoles, tout en contribuant à la sécurité et à l’autosuffisance alimentaires. Cette démarche s’inscrit également dans la vision de développement socio-économique portée par le programme SIMANDOU 2040, qui ambitionne de transformer durablement les secteurs stratégiques de l’économie guinéenne. La planification, le suivi et l’évaluation au cœur des échanges Durant ces cinq jours de travaux, les participants ont approfondi plusieurs thématiques essentielles à l’amélioration de la gestion du secteur agricole. Les modules ont notamment porté sur le suivi-évaluation, la rédaction administrative, l’éthique et la déontologie dans le secteur public, la planification agricole et la gestion axée sur les résultats, ainsi que la gouvernance agricole, la coordination territoriale et les politiques publiques. Les participants ont également bénéficié de présentations consacrées à des outils et stratégies nationaux, notamment la politique foncière agricole, la stratégie nationale de développement de la riziculture de deuxième génération, la plateforme numérique de gestion des intrants agricoles « AGRINEMA » et la stratégie nationale de fourniture durable des intrants aux producteurs. Ces différents modules visaient à permettre aux responsables agricoles de mieux maîtriser les instruments de planification et de pilotage, d’améliorer la coordination entre les différents niveaux de l’administration et de renforcer la transparence dans la gestion des activités. Une approche participative axée sur les résultats Pour garantir l’efficacité des apprentissages, la formation a reposé sur une méthodologie participative combinant exposés théoriques, exercices pratiques, études de cas, témoignages de praticiens, travaux de groupe et discussions en plénière. Trois consultants ont été mobilisés pour accompagner le processus, avec l’appui de responsables techniques appelés à partager leurs connaissances et leur expérience dans les domaines relevant de leurs compétences. Au-delà de l’acquisition de connaissances, cette approche visait également à développer les capacités de travail en équipe, à favoriser les synergies entre les services et à améliorer la communication professionnelle au sein de l’administration agricole. À l’issue de la session, les résultats attendus portaient notamment sur le renforcement des compétences en planification et en suivi-évaluation, une meilleure compréhension des liens entre les différentes étapes de gestion des politiques agricoles et l'initiation des participants à la conception d’un dispositif de suivi-évaluation de la Campagne agricole 2026-2027. Un enjeu stratégique pour la souveraineté alimentaire de la Guinée À travers cette initiative, le ministère de l’Agriculture réaffirme l’importance du renforcement des capacités humaines et institutionnelles dans la conduite des politiques agricoles nationales. En effet, la réussite d’une campagne agricole ne dépend pas uniquement de la disponibilité des terres, des semences, des engrais ou des équipements. Elle repose également sur la capacité des responsables à planifier les interventions, à mobiliser efficacement les ressources, à accompagner les producteurs et à mesurer les résultats obtenus. Le renforcement des compétences des directeurs régionaux, préfectoraux et communaux constitue ainsi un investissement stratégique pour améliorer les performances du secteur agricole et assurer une meilleure mise en œuvre des politiques publiques sur l’ensemble du territoire national. En définitive, la formation organisée du 12 au 16 octobre 2026 à Tindo traduit la volonté de faire de la planification rigoureuse, du suivi-évaluation et de la bonne gouvernance des piliers de la transformation agricole en Guinée. Un engagement qui prend tout son sens dans la perspective de la Campagne agricole 2026-2027 et de l’ambition nationale de mieux produire pour mieux nourrir les populations guinéennes.
